newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 11.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Instant fines for crimes proposed: People caught smoking cannabis could be among minor offenders given instant fine notices instead of appearing in courts under a proposal being examined by police. Page 1.

Leaders wait as Kirton weighs plans: Dumped Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton will say on Tuesday morning whether he plans to rob the government of its one-seat majority by quitting junior Coalition partner NZ First. Page 1.

Superannuation pamphlet worried panel: Papers made public by the Labour Party show that the superannuation referendum panel was concerned about the government sending households a pamphlet on superannuation. Page 2.

Clark hints talks with Alliance may start again: Talks between the Alliance and Labour on forming a common approach to issues are likely to begin again, with Labour leader Helen Clark saying the two parties' leadership need to "get their heads together" on superannuation. Page 2.
Hide moves on travel perks: ACT NZ MP Rodney Hide has prepared a private member's bill to remove the travel subsidy for former MPs and their spouses. Page 2.

Warehouse covers falling Kiwi till after Christmas: Discount retailer The Warehouse said that its forward foreign exchange cover meant it would not be affected by the falling New Zealand dollar till after Christmas. Page 15.

Dollar not expected to increase import prices: Prices of imported goods were not likely to rise sharply after the recent fall in the value of the New Zealand dollar, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell chief economist Ulf Schoefisch, said Friday. Page 16.
THE PRESS
Armed raids increase staff fears: A surge in armed robberies in Christchurch has alarmed workers at businesses most likely to be targeted by thieves.

Minister plugs sex strategy in schools: Making free condoms available in schools and youth clubs is not government policy but needs to be seriously considered, Youth Affairs Minister Deborah Morris says.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Fears for babies' health: Early discharge policy under scrutiny: Newborn babies could be getting sicker because their mothers are being sent home from hospital earlier.

Disappointing sales hurt furniture chain: The retailing group Farmers-Deka is believed to be reconsidering the future of the Freedom Furniture chain in New Zealand, following weaker than expected sales.

Peters plan could help economy - Dr Savings: The Retirement Savings Scheme promoted by Treasurer Winston Peters could have significant benefits for the economy, says a visiting Australian superannuation expert.

Telecom fails on exec test: Only a minority of senior executives rate Telecom New Zealand as their preferred carrier for domestic long distance and international calls, according to the latest Business Herald/University of Auckland survey.

Rivals cooperate on spadework: Companies that are usually fierce rivals in the forestry sector are splicing together a long-term strategy report on their industry to help secure government research and development funding.
Evergreen still on lookout for more forests: Evergreen Forests is considering several investments to increase its forestry estate, says chief executive Mark Bogle.
